The draw matched the chances fairly well: the model gave a draw the single largest probability at 47%, with Crowmoor slightly more likely than Ashvale to win.
md01-ash-crw.decided: The turning point was Mikel Carbajosa’s 45+3 strike, a chance worth 0.16 xG. When the match engine froze the moment the shot was struck and replayed the rest of the game 20 times as it went in, Crowmoor won 90% of those simulated finishes and none were home wins; when the shot was instead saved in the alternate 20 simulations Crowmoor still won 60% while home wins rose to 10%. That swing pushed the outcome strongly towards Crowmoor, but given the stated 22% margin of error the game could plausibly have gone either way.

Marin Radošević pulled one back for Westmere in the 65th and Kingsport finished with ten men after Cian Brennan was sent off in the 75th; expected goals were 1.43 for Kingsport and 0.41 for Westmere, and the result broadly matched the chances created. Shots favoured Kingsport 14 to 4 while both sides managed three on target, and Arakawa was rightly named player of the match with two goals.
md09-kin-wes.decided: The turning point came early: Yuto Arakawa's 4th-minute strike, an xG 0.11 chance, set the game on its course. When the match was frozen at that instant and played 20 times as it happened, Kingsport won in 95% of those futures; when the shot was flipped to a save in 20 alternate plays, Kingsport's win probability fell to 40% and the most common flipped final score was 0-0, a swing well outside the 22% margin of error, so that early goal was decisive.
